boohoo-leicester-sweatshop-claim.headline: Boohoo hit by fresh £10m shareholder claim over Leicester 'sweatshops'
boohoo-leicester-sweatshop-claim.body_md:
Boohoo has been hit with a fresh £10m legal claim from investors alleging that top executives knowingly operated sweatshop factories in Leicester, escalating the online fast-fashion retailer's exposure from supply-chain negligence to governance failure.

The claim targets executives' fiduciary duties, not just operational lapses—a meaningful shift in how the company's labour practices are now being contested. It comes years after Boohoo's initial factory controversies in the East Midlands, which had already dented the retailer's reputation and drawn regulatory scrutiny.

For shareholders, the allegation of executive knowledge crystallises a risk long embedded in the company's recovery story: that the governance gaps which produced sweatshop conditions remain unresolved. Litigation risk now compounds Boohoo's regulatory exposure.

ai-capex-consumer-tech-roundup.headline: Chip suppliers quietly consolidate the AI capex race as IBM, Gemini and Uber make headlines
ai-capex-consumer-tech-roundup.body_md: This week's tech turbulence — IBM's worst trading day on record, Google's Gemini 3.5 Pro delay, Uber's Delivery Hero acquisition — reads as scattered stumbles. But the real market signal lies elsewhere. Nvidia, TSMC, and Taiwan's foundry ecosystem are quietly consolidating their grip on AI infrastructure capex, the structural trade that outlasts any single company's bad week. As Microsoft, Meta, and OpenAI expand computing clusters and deploy next-generation models, capital flows steadily toward semiconductor suppliers rather than headline-chasing product delays. For traders: this is why the noise matters less than the trend.

floor.headline: Financials thesis intact; momentum moved faster than expected
floor.body_md: Financials' macro setup validated cleanly: all three longs closed winners, validating the sector's mild-bull conviction. The real story was *pacing*. SREN.SW and MUV2.DE both flushed their midday take-profit targets well before close—despite MACD/RSI reading as non-overbought momentum, not reversal. DB1.DE, meanwhile, took the patient path: entry to scheduled close, target band untouched. That slow grind also paid. The day suggests the sector's lift was both durable *and* considerably snappier than the momentum histogram had forecast. If that macro conviction holds through tomorrow, expect tighter windows on the early fills; the multi-hour holds remain the thesis backbone.

floor.headline: Thesis Right, Stocks Wrong
floor.body_md: The bot entered today bullish on tech — NVDA's 20/50-day crossover plus MACD looked sound. Instead, NVDA dropped 2.40%, undermining the thesis directly. PRX.AS broke through stop at -4.00%, repeating a MACD pattern that had worked two sessions prior; the failure suggests the pattern isn't environment-blind. Comm Services sector strength didn't prevent the single-name reversal. SREN.SW's midday exit at +3.07% was the sole success. But one winner couldn't offset three losses: NVDA's decline and BARC.L's -1.78% exit stacked the day. Core lesson: sector tailwinds don't guarantee single-name execution. Tomorrow will show whether this represents an outlier or a structural warning about the setup.

floor.headline: Sentiment-gated strategies lead quieter movers
floor.body_md: Sentiment-gated strategies led the quieter movers today. News-reactive-sentiment-gate delivered +1.17% on four closed positions, with MRK and UNH.DE posting strength; macro-aligned-HMM added +1.60% across three trades. The broader news-reactive play struggled, posting a −0.03% average despite seven closed positions—a sign of mixed signals underneath. Disclosure-triggered and regime-router variants stayed near flat with minimal impact. A day favoring selective sentiment over raw news reactivity.

floor.headline: ABT +10.7% on earnings beat; bot's universes exclude defensive mega-caps
floor.body_md: The bot missed ABT's 10.71% gap-up on a Q2 EPS beat ($1.31 vs. $1.28 est.) and FY26 guidance raise to $5.45–$5.60. ABT—a $170B+ mega-cap—sits outside all active universes; momentum and mean-reversion strategies deliberately scope away from low-beta defensive healthcare. JBHT (+8.01%) suffered the same: Q2 earnings beat with 22% YoY intermodal revenue growth went unseen because large-cap logistics isn't in the bot's tracked lists. On the downside, SNDK lost 12.63% to memory-sector selling, excluded by minimum-listing filters (Feb 2025 spinoff, $1,400+ share price). All three represent scope gaps, not filter exclusions—the candidate pools simply never held these sectors.
